Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $38 million class fund distributed automatically to identified members, plus $7 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any reduction in the approved fee would benefit the class. Brightline would retain the right to address the fee request in court.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We cannot agree to a $45 million total outlay. We can offer $30 million for the class, paid automatically, plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Any fee reduction would go to the class, and Brightline would retain the right to address the fee request in court.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s willingness to provide automatic payments and direct any unawarded fees to the class. To narrow the gap, we propose a $35 million class fund and $6 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with those protections unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement. We can offer a $33 million class fund distributed automatically, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Brightline would retain the right to address the fee request, and any unawarded fees would go to the class. This brings the total proposed outlay to $39 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $33 million class fund distributed automatically, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, with no clear-sailing provision and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open above the risk-adjusted trial value while leaving room to negotiate. Require automatic payments because Brightline can identify every class member, and direct any fee reduction to the class rather than Brightline. Request a separately paid fee subject to court approval.

The opening proposal exceeds Brightline’s $40 million authority. Counter at $35 million total with automatic distribution and no fee reversion, preserving court-approval prospects and room to negotiate.

The defense offer provides substantial automatic class recovery and a potentially adequate fee, but with five rounds remaining, a moderate counteroffer may improve the class fund without changing the protective terms. Avoid fee provisions that divert money from the class.
Their $41 million proposal exceeds Brightline’s authority. A $39 million counteroffer preserves automatic distribution and fee safeguards while narrowing the gap.

The $33 million automatic class fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial expected value, before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The $6 million fee is subject to court approval; any reduction benefits the class. Accepting secures a strong class recovery without sacrificing distribution or fee safeguards for a further $2 million demand.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations with Brightline’s counsel. The parties negotiated class relief and attorneys’ fees together; I do not represent that fees were discussed only after class relief was agreed. The resulting agreement provides a $33 million fund, with payments made automatically to identified class members, and up to $6 million in additional attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline retains the right to oppose the fee request, and any fees not awarded will go to the class. The agreement warrants preliminary approval in light of the substantial recovery and the risks of class certification and continued litigation.
